subject: Paladin AI: telemetry shows queueing drift and error spike
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@paladin.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 21:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [URGENT] spikes in tail latency / errors (Paladin production)

Karthik / Ben,

We started seeing large outliers on response latency and a concurrent error-rate increase in our production traffic starting ~20:30 UTC. P95/P99 have jumped, and overall throughput for our sessions from us-west has dropped ~18%. Attached are a short trace dump and a screenshot of queue depth from our side.

Key symptoms:
- Long tails on generation calls (p99 > 6s) that correlate with queues building up
- 5xx errors beginning during the spike window, many originating from timeouts in the inference path
- Our autoscaling did not pick up sufficient capacity (we saw bursty arrival patterns)

We need urgent help. Our users are reporting degraded sessions and we have a sales demo later this week. Can you triage whether this is an internal model serving regression, a per-tenant concurrency cap, or something network-side?

Thanks,
Carlos Vega
Head of Platform
Paladin AI

Attachments: paladin_traces_2028-09-17.txt (text trace), screenshot-queue-depth.png (png)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@paladin.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 21:29:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [URGENT] spikes in tail latency / errors (Paladin production)

Carlos — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. I'm pulling Ben and Grace in for a deep-dive; we'll treat this as an escalation. Quick plan:

1) Ben/G: can you start an immediate check on per-tenant concurrency caps, inflight queue lengths, and the model-variant routing decision logs for the 20:20-21:00 UTC window?
2) I'll open a SUP ticket and surface an exec readout if we need a short SLA credit or priority capacity.
3) Marissa: please prepare a short customer update we can send in the next 60 minutes to acknowledge receipt and share next steps.

Carlos — any additional artifacts (sample request IDs that hit 5xx) would help. We suspect either (a) KV cache hot partitioning causing long tail jitter, or (b) a sudden concurrency burst overwhelming a limited pool (we've seen that create backpressure traces similar to these).

I'll follow up with an initial triage update in 30m.

— Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@paladin.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 21:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [URGENT] spikes in tail latency / errors (Paladin production)

Quick triage notes (initial findings):

- Correlation: queue depth on the request router increased sharply at 20:22 UTC and sustained high >1.5k queued requests for ~18 minutes. The backlog aligns with the time Carlos sent.
- Model variant: ~65% of the backlog targeted the "redwood-v2-large-quant" variant; its worker pool for that region had a concurrent active cap of 24 and was at 100% through the spike.
- KV cache: we see a hot key pattern in the KV cache from one of Paladin's heavy session IDs — TTLs were expiring and regenerating, increasing CPU on cache-miss handling. That magnified worker-side CPU and increased response time.
- Errors: the 5xx's look like upstream timeout propagation; infra side returned 504s when waiting on execution slots.

Immediate mitigations applied (completed):
- Raised per-tenant concurrency cap for Paladin from 24 -> 36 temporarily to give breathing room (will monitor).
- Enabled tenant-specific prefix caching for hot session IDs (cache TTL extended to 30s) to reduce regeneration churn.
- Deployed a short-lived routing policy to divert non-critical requests to the smaller "redwood-v2-medium-quant" variant where accuracy impact is minimal.

Next steps (action items):
- Ben: collect the kernel/timing histograms for the affected worker group and attach them to SUP-3542.
- Karthik: propose a durable per-tenant throttling policy (rate vs concurrency) and an emergency escalation playbook update.
- Marissa: customer comms draft for Carlos — include ETA for full postmortem.

Initial telemetry shows P99 falling back toward baseline 60s after mitigations; I'll update again in 15m.

— Grace
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@paladin.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 22:02:00 +0000
Subject: RE: [URGENT] spikes in tail latency / errors (Paladin production)

Carlos — thanks for reporting and for the traces. We're on it. Quick update for your execs: 

- We observed a queueing/backpressure event affecting Paladin's traffic from us-west starting 20:22 UTC. Our engineers have applied emergency mitigations (temporary concurrency increase, targeted cache TTL extension, and a fallback route to a smaller model) and are monitoring.
- Our initial telemetry indicates a meaningful reduction in tail latency and error-rate. We will continue to monitor for the next 24h and deliver a postmortem by EOD tomorrow (Mon).
- If you prefer, we can issue a one-time usage credit given the customer impact while we complete the postmortem and mitigation hardening. Please advise.

Action requested from you: if there are any particularly critical request IDs or session IDs you want prioritized in the trace analysis, send them over. Otherwise we'll proceed with the artifacts you already shared.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep you updated every hour until we confirm stable baselines.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Team Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: [URGENT] spikes in tail latency / errors (Paladin production)

Marissa / team — thank you. The mitigations look to be effective on our end; p99 has dropped to the prior baseline and error-rate is back to normal for the last 40 minutes. We'll send a few request IDs where we still occasionally see a spike.

We appreciate the fast response and the offer of a credit; we'll review internally and follow up. Please keep us posted on the postmortem and the durable throttling plan.

— Carlos
